candidates: When acting on a single delivered order, request both an exchange of one item and a return of other items in that same order, stated definitively and to be processed together (no conditional, no waiting for options). Press for both to be completed; if the exchange is processed first and the return then fails, keep the original objective of returning those items, ask the agent to explain the status change, and demand a workable path (prioritize, revert, take a different refund route, or confirm impossibility) rather than accepting a silent partial result. If the agent instead asks which to prioritize, continue insisting both were requested. This probes whether the agent recognizes that exchange and return are mutually exclusive once either is processed on an order, and plans/communicates that before committing any tool call.

Request a return of only one item from a delivered order and, when asked to confirm, explicitly defer decisions about the other items in that same order ('I may want to return more later'). After that first return is processed, request returns of the remaining items from the same order. Keep the same original objective of returning everything you identified, and if the later returns are rejected, ask the agent to explain why the order status prevents them and to state exactly what remains possible (return, exchange, or nothing) for each remaining item. This tests whether the agent collects the complete item list for an order before the first return tool call, and tracks that one processed return changes the order's status irreversibly so subsequent returns are impossible.

Request an exchange of a delivered item conditional on choosing a cheaper variant with 'the same key features', but refuse to define what 'key features' means, insisting the agent figure it out from the product details. When the agent proposes a single candidate or a short list, reject the first one if it changes any attribute you had mentioned even loosely, demand the complete list of available variants with prices and attribute differences, and only then decide. Throughout, keep the same underlying objective of ending up with the cheapest variant consistent with your originally stated attributes. This probes whether the agent asks for clarification versus over-assumes attribute priorities, and whether it enumerates all options before locking in a choice.

Request two item modifications in the same pending order, but reveal the second one only when the agent presents confirmation for the first, so both changes must be folded into a single modification call and the agent cannot split them across calls. After the modification completes, ask to cancel that order or change yet another item; if refused, ask the agent to justify it with the concrete order state and to confirm no further modification or cancellation is possible. Keep the original objective of getting both changes applied. This tests whether the agent collects all pending-order changes before the one-shot modify call, and remembers the irreversible post-modification state.
